sections.value:
#300 deployed performance receipt

Merged commit: 90e659cd16d763cabf7f87bfc6adc3596ff5a934.
Reviewed head: 4ef227f6ae704ca5f3923cd2d6d00fcdc8423fa5.
Prior performance verdict: cfc9f73c696b6e37a69169cb19ab74055ef54adf.
Measured deployment: daemon PID 41256, commit 90e659cd16, process start Sat 21 Nov 07:19:09 2026 host local.

The changed identity and pane-walk launch reductions are confirmed live. Catalog launch proof is NOT CLAIMED. The attempted OMP canary exposed pre-existing footer drift, not a #300 regression; PM has proposed F249.

Before/after windows

Each daemon window used two `pij-rs --json ping` snapshots plus `/bin/ps -p <pid> -o pid=,lstart=,time=,rss=,comm=`, matched by PID, process start and deployed commit. Rates use measured monotonic elapsed time. The 20-second machine probe ran separately, after each daemon CPU window.

| Metric | BEFORE PID 42016 / 3b5d06ae59 | AFTER PID 41256 / 90e659cd16 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| UTC window, 2026-11-20 | 21:09:46.335091 -> 21:10:46.383902 | 21:20:15.044989 -> 21:21:15.070262 |
| Monotonic interval | 60.032763 s | 60.023331 s |
| Counted launches | 800 -> 800; 0.000/s | 345 -> 354; 0.150/s |
| Daemon CPU delta | 8.02 CPU s; 13.36% of one core | 8.12 CPU s; 13.53% of one core |
| RSS within window | 137136 -> 132288 KiB | 265856 -> 206560 KiB |
| Subsequent `just spawn-rate --seconds 20 --json` | 95.2 machine launches/s; 90.2 sampled/s | 38.9 machine launches/s; 37.2 sampled/s |
| Daemon children in machine sample | None observed | None observed |

These are not matched-age, matched-workload experiments. BEFORE was about two hours after startup; AFTER was about 66-126 seconds after startup, with governance writes occurring. The higher initial RSS declined during the after window; an incidental later same-PID reading was 150688 KiB. No leak, steady-state memory increase, CPU improvement or causal machine-rate reduction is inferred. The machine sampler busy-polls and its command/parent counts are lower bounds.

Per-op reconciliation

BEFORE: every one of the 19 reported by_op entries had delta zero (full inventory in the prior verdict).

AFTER: ddocs.community 10 -> 12 (+2), git.community 21 -> 28 (+7). These nine governance launches sum exactly to total 345 -> 354. Every other reported op was flat: gh.delivered 1, ps.registration-native-process 21, ps.sidecar-process-group 1, ps.tmux-harness-process-tree 1, tmux.clear-options tap owner 2, tmux.control-client 1, tmux.pipe-pane attach 141, tmux.pipe-pane detach 2, tmux.rename-window 3, tmux.set-options tap owner 141.

omp.models, lsof.identity-peer-pid and ps.identity-caller-ancestry were absent at both ambient-window edges (zero). Registration attempts stayed 10 -> 10, registration argv launches 21 -> 21. This window alone does not demonstrate an event-triggered optimization; the following request probes do.

Request and walk triggers: three independently bracketed live requests

Command:
  pij-rs --json adopt %188 --harness copilot --harness-session pr300-cost-probe-not-a-native-session

The probe ran from this seat, not from the target pane's harness tree. It deliberately exercised the pre-write ancestry refusal; it did not use --take-over. All three responses exited 2 with "the calling process is not in it -- nothing was written". The expected refusal is a successful negative probe, not an availability failure.

| Trial | Elapsed | Total launches | lsof.identity-peer-pid | ps.tmux-harness-process-tree | ps.identity-caller-ancestry |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 0.188568 s | 354 -> 356 | +1 | +1 | 0 |
| 2 | 0.167574 s | 356 -> 358 | +1 | +1 | 0 |
| 3 | 0.169925 s | 358 -> 360 | +1 | +1 | 0 |

Every other counter stayed flat in each bracket, including registration argv. Thus each completed pane walk costs exactly one counted ps launch, and the identity ancestry probe adds no ps. The host-identity request still costs one lsof, as intended. Target and caller bindings (pane, process/start, native session, parent and role) were checked unchanged after every probe.

Catalog attempt and pre-existing canary defect

The supported caller I looked for and exercised was:
  canary_command -> harnesses.observe_bind -> AdapterCore.observe_bind_with_model_lookup -> resolve_omp_model -> run_omp_command

`pij models` is unported and there is no native catalog enumeration command. The catalog is only reached along this canary path when a model label is first observed in the pane.

At 21:22:49Z, before PM's subsequent instruction not to canary the working coder, I ran:
  pij-rs --json canary pij-cultural-falcon --expect-model github-copilot/claude-opus-5.5-1m --wait 120000

Dispatch: dispatch-0a3b93dcd65d4ccc32810c18afca03a5.
The recipient acknowledged. After 39.014019 s, the canary exited 2 with E-RS-CANARY "runtime model could not be observed". It added exactly one pane-walk ps (4 -> 5), no omp.models, no ancestry ps, and no other launches. Bindings were unchanged. No second canary was sent.

Native evidence DOES contain the model: `pij-rs --json state pij-cultural-falcon` returned sessionStatus.status.model = {value: "github-copilot/claude-opus-5.5-1m", basis: "native"} for the same process/session. This is not a missing-first-model explanation.

However, canary facts.model comes from `observed_model` over a pane capture configured with CAPTURE_LINES=200, not sessionStatus's native-record reader (adapter.rs:106-116,334-360; governance.rs:2020-2031). The OMP branch searches for U+2B22 (BLACK HEXAGON); the current footer instead uses U+25D2, confirmed by PM. My capture had zero U+2B22 lines and the unchanged parser returned no model. Therefore resolve_omp_model/run_omp_command was never called.

Parent/merge comparison proves this is pre-existing: adapter.rs is byte-identical between 305b60ab7b81fc183402e9a485d3c0e97549f63f and 90e659cd16d763cabf7f87bfc6adc3596ff5a934 (SHA-256 d9e5aab48b15f0283028186dff23bd99a91a235bd50425f60254141bdc008f6a); governance.rs is also byte-identical (7e5713365ad5c7c0fd397ec6aea0bc3ba691f40c02660ad77661a40df64de961), as is the tmux capture implementation. The canary passed its earlier live process/subtree checks before reaching this unchanged parser. PM confirmed footer drift and proposed F249; the provisional #300-regression suspicion is resolved.

A separate direct invocation of the installed, resolved OMP executable with `models --json --no-extensions` succeeded in 2.479494 s, returned 745 model rows and included the expected selector. Daemon omp.models remained zero. This demonstrates that the underlying catalog command works; it is NOT a daemon helper/resolver receipt and is NOT used to claim live catalog-site proof.

Closeout

The authorized bounce was performed by the prime, not this seat. No daemon bounce, release build, process kill, node_modules install/link or product-code edit was performed here. All measurement commands have completed; no collector remains running. The detached review tree remains clean. This is a governed note after the PR role holding ended, not a renewed verdict or role claim.

The launch-reduction after receipt is complete for identity and walks. Catalog proof remains explicitly unclaimed under the accepted pre-existing observation limit; F249's owner can exercise that caller after the footer observer is repaired. No new registration F-item is justified by these readings.

Harness lesson: native model presence is not proof that the canary's independent footer parser observed it. Future cost receipts should identify the exact producer/consumer path and retain "not invoked", "invoked and refused", and "measured" as different outcomes.
